outcomes.text: The interdisciplinary program aims to develop critical and creative scientific reasoning.
The program develops knowledge of ecology, evolution and their computational study.

courses.name: First Year Seminar
courses.description: Supports university transition, community connections and student planning.

category_review.locator: CS 1200 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: University transition, resource use and personal planning fall outside the subject-matter categories; no programming content is established.

courses.name: First-Year Interdisciplinary Seminar
courses.description: Explores global citizenship, university resources and interdisciplinary problem solving.

category_review.locator: INPR 1000 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The first-year seminar emphasizes university resources and personal/academic development with global-challenge context, without a sufficiently specified substantive subject for this taxonomy.

courses.name: Science at Northeastern
courses.description: Introduces science students to university study, academic skills and their college community.

category_review.locator: INSC 1000 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course introduces college/university resources, academic skills and community transition; a Science host does not establish scientific domain instruction.

courses.name: Professional Development for Khoury Co-op
courses.description: Prepares students for co-op applications, interviews and workplace expectations.

category_review.locator: CS 1210 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Co-op preparation, resumes, interviews and workplace conduct do not establish a primary computing subject category.

courses.name: Professional Development for Co-op
courses.description: Prepares students for co-op searches, interviewing, professional practice and career decisions.

category_review.locator: EESC 2000 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course teaches co-op procedures, job search, professional behavior and career decisions; it does not establish a disciplinary scientific curriculum.

courses.name: Introduction to Program Design and Implementation
courses.description: Introduces programming, dataset analysis and ethical issues in software design.

category_review.locator: CS 2000 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The course teaches program construction, coding and introductory data processing to students without programming experience.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2000
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting introductory programming coursework.

category_review.locator: CS 2001 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the introductory program-design course and practices its computing topics.

courses.name: Program Design and Implementation 1
courses.description: Develops program design, object-oriented abstractions and software engineering practices.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CS 2100 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Data/object-oriented design, data structures, abstraction, testing and software construction are the central methods.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2100
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting program design coursework.

category_review.locator: CS 2101 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the reviewed program-design and software-construction course.

courses.name: Advanced Programming with Data
courses.description: Develops robust software architectures and data pipelines using substantial datasets.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 3500 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Software architectures, reusable APIs, testing and maintainable data pipelines center on general software design and implementation.

courses.name: Introduction to Databases
courses.description: Develops relational database design, SQL and introductory database-system techniques.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or EECE 2560 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CS 3200 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Relational database design, query processing, indexing, concurrency and recovery are database-system methods.

courses.name: Introduction to Mathematical Reasoning
courses.description: Develops proof writing and mathematical reasoning using sets, relations and functions.

category_review.locator: MATH 1365 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Mathematical proof, logical argument, sets, relations and functions are explicitly the focus.

courses.name: Intensive Mathematical Reasoning
courses.description: Intensively develops proofs, mathematical structures, cardinality and introductory algebra.

category_review.locator: MATH 1465 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Proof techniques, sets, cardinality, algebra and group theory provide mathematical reasoning.

courses.name: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Studies the mathematical basis of AI through linear algebra, probability and computational exercises.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 3000 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The description explicitly emphasizes linear algebra, probability and numerical mathematical foundations, using AI as their motivating application.

courses.name: Information Presentation and Visualization
courses.description: Studies how to design, implement and evaluate visual representations of data.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4200 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Visualization combines programming, perception, visual communication and domain presentation; the description does not establish one defensible primary category among these.

courses.name: Large-Scale Information Storage and Retrieval
courses.description: Studies scalable data storage, distributed databases and retrieval methods.
courses.prerequisites: ( CS 3100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 310M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 3500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 3500 with a minimum grade of D- ); CS 3200 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4300 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Distributed databases, storage architectures, reliability and data retrieval are computing infrastructure methods.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.description: Introduces predictive modeling and major supervised and unsupervised learning methods.
courses.prerequisites: DS 3000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 250M with a minimum grade of D- or ( MATH 2331 with a minimum grade of D- ; MATH 3081 with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: DS 4400 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Supervised and unsupervised learning, predictive models, model evaluation and learning algorithms are the explicit central content.

courses.name: Embedded Design: Enabling Robotics
courses.description: Combines digital design, programming and embedded systems to control robotic devices.
courses.prerequisites: EECE 2140 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: EECE 2160 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The description integrates digital hardware design, object-oriented programming/Linux and a robotic-device project without establishing one dominant subject among systems, programming and domain implementation. The robotics example does not establish an AI-method course.

courses.name: Fundamentals of Digital Design and Computer Organization
courses.description: Develops digital logic, computer architecture and hardware models for a simple processor.
courses.prerequisites: EECE 2160 with a minimum grade of D- or EECE 2310 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: EECE 2322 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Logic circuits, instruction-set architecture, processor construction, hardware-description languages and assembly interfaces establish computer architecture/digital systems as the primary subject.

courses.name: Digital, Analytics, Technology, and Automation Research Practicum
courses.description: Applies analytics, digital technology and machine learning to client problems through a research practicum.

category_review.locator: MKTG 4606 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The practicum centers on solving client business/organizational problems with digital technology and analytics, combining technical and managerial practice. Machine learning is one stated tool, not evidence that a fixed AI algorithm curriculum dominates every project.

courses.name: Foundations in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
courses.description: Introduces ecology and evolution through lectures, field investigation and independent research.

courses.name: Lab for EEMB 1101
courses.description: Investigates foundational ecology and evolution through experiments.

courses.name: Foundations in Ecological and Evolutionary Genomics
courses.description: Introduces molecular ecology, genomic analysis and computational and laboratory methods.

courses.name: Lab for EEMB 1105
courses.description: Tests ecological and evolutionary hypotheses using molecular-ecology laboratory methods.

courses.name: Genetics and Molecular Biology
courses.description: Examines inheritance and gene function through molecular and population approaches.
courses.prerequisites: ( BIOL 1111 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 2299 with a minimum grade of D- or EEMB 1105 with a minimum grade of D- or EEMB 2400 with a minimum grade of D- ); ( CHEM 1151 with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 233M with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 1161 with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 1211 with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 1217 with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: BIOL 2301 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Inheritance, gene/genome function, developmental genetics and molecular biological methods are substantive biological science; computational tools are part of this domain work.

courses.name: Lab for BIOL 2301
courses.description: Investigates genetics through laboratory methods and analysis of experimental data.
courses.prerequisites: BIOL 2301 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: BIOL 2302 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The laboratory investigates and analyzes genetics/molecular biology from BIOL 2301.

courses.name: Introduction to Evolution
courses.description: Examines evolutionary mechanisms, adaptation and the history of life using scientific evidence.
courses.prerequisites: BIOL 1107 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 1111 with a minimum grade of D- or EEMB 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1400 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Ecology
courses.description: Studies ecological processes through research, experimentation and scientific communication.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C

courses.name: Lab for EEMB 2302
courses.description: Investigates ecology concepts through laboratory experiments.

courses.name: Senior Thesis
courses.description: Develops a faculty-supervised undergraduate thesis.

courses.name: Human Parasitology
courses.description: Examines human parasites, their life cycles, transmission and disease effects.
courses.prerequisites: BIOL 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 1107 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 1111 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 1115 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: BIOL 2327 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Parasite biology, life cycles, transmission and pathogenesis are biological/health domain content.

courses.name: Plant Biology
courses.description: Examines plant structure, physiology, diversity and responses to climate change.
courses.prerequisites: BIOL 1107 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 1111 with a minimum grade of D- or EEMB 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or EEMB 1105 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1400 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Marine Biology
courses.description: Examines marine organisms, ecosystem processes and biological research.
courses.prerequisites: ( BIOL 1107 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 1111 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 1115 with a minimum grade of D- or EEMB 1101 with a minimum grade of D- ); (ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C )

courses.name: Lab for EEMB 2700
courses.description: Investigates marine biology through discussion and laboratory experiments.

courses.name: Ecological and Conservation Genomics
courses.description: Applies ecological genetics and computational analysis to conservation problems.
courses.prerequisites: BIOL 2301 with a minimum grade of C- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of C- or ECON 2350 with a minimum grade of C- or BUSM 22EM with a minimum grade of C- or EEMB 2400 with a minimum grade of C- or ENVR 2500 with a minimum grade of C- or MATH 3081 with a minimum grade of C-

courses.name: Wildlife Ecology
courses.description: Studies wildlife populations, habitats and conservation using data and ecological models.
courses.prerequisites: EEMB 2302 with a minimum grade of C

courses.name: Animal Behavior
courses.description: Examines animal behavior through physiological, ecological, genetic and evolutionary explanations.
courses.prerequisites: BIOL 1113 with a minimum grade of D or BIOL 2299 with a minimum grade of D or EEMB 1105 with a minimum grade of D

courses.name: Plants and Society
courses.description: Examines useful plants, their biology, cultural roles and sustainable management.
courses.prerequisites: EEMB 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVM 115M with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1400 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Lab for ENVR 3800
courses.description: Develops plant observation, identification and care through practical laboratory work.

courses.name: Conservation Biology
courses.description: Applies ecological and evolutionary principles to biodiversity conservation and restoration.
courses.prerequisites: BIOL 1107 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 1111 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 1115 with a minimum grade of D- or EEMB 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or EEMB 2302 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVM 115M with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1400 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Landscape and Restoration Ecology
courses.description: Examines landscapes, ecosystem disturbance and restoration through spatial and ecological analysis.
courses.prerequisites: BIOL 1107 with a minimum grade of C or BIOL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or EEMB 1101 with a minimum grade of C or ENVR 1101 with a minimum grade of C or ENVM 115M with a minimum grade of C or ENVR 1400 with a minimum grade of C

courses.name: Global Oceanic Change
courses.description: Examines ocean change across timescales and its environmental and social implications.
courses.prerequisites: Additional course-description condition: one laboratory science course or permission of instructor.

courses.name: Food Security and Sustainability
courses.description: Examines sustainable food production, climate pressures, nutrition and food security.
courses.prerequisites: EEMB 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVM 115M with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1110 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1120 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1200 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1400 with a minimum grade of D- or SOCL 1246 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Wetlands
courses.description: Examines wetland processes, ecosystems, societal values and management.
courses.prerequisites: EEMB 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVM 115M with a minimum grade of D- or EEMB 2302 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1200 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1400 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Streams and Watershed Ecology
courses.description: Studies stream and watershed ecology through theory, management questions and field methods.
courses.prerequisites: EEMB 2302 with a minimum grade of C- or ENVR 1400 with a minimum grade of C-

courses.name: Urban Ecology
courses.description: Examines urban ecosystems, biodiversity, ecosystem services and future environmental pressures.
courses.prerequisites: EEMB 2302 with a minimum grade of C- or ENVR 1101 with a minimum grade of C- or ENVM 115M with a minimum grade of C- or ENVR 1200 with a minimum grade of C- or ENVR 1400 with a minimum grade of C- or graduate program admission

courses.name: Population Dynamics
courses.description: Develops mathematical population models and tests their dynamics and predictions using R.
courses.prerequisites: (( MATH 1241 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1251 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1341 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 21EM (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- ); (ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C )) or graduate program admission

courses.name: Geographic Information Systems
courses.description: Develops GIS data collection, visualization and spatial analysis through applied research.
courses.prerequisites: EEMB 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVM 115M with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1200 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1400 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 2200 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Lab for ENVR 3300
courses.description: Applies geographic-information-system concepts through laboratory exercises.

courses.name: Advanced Biostatistics
courses.description: Develops advanced statistical modeling for biological systems using R.
courses.prerequisites: ENVR 2500 with a minimum grade of C- or graduate program admission

courses.name: Advanced Spatial Analysis
courses.description: Examines advanced GIS, spatial statistics and computational representations of geographic data.
courses.prerequisites: ENVR 3300 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 5260 with a minimum grade of C- or ENVR 5260 with a minimum grade of C-

courses.name: Biostatistics
courses.description: Develops probability, inference and experimental design for biological data analysis.

category_review.locator: ENVR 2500 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The source explicitly centers mathematical foundations of statistics, probability, inference, estimation and parametric/nonparametric tests. Biological data provide the application context, not a different primary subject.

courses.name: Lab for ENVR 2500
courses.description: Applies biostatistical methods through supervised R laboratory exercises.

category_review.locator: ENVR 2501 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The laboratory accompanies the explicitly statistical ENVR 2500 and applies its statistical topics in R; using a programming environment does not make the primary subject general software construction.

courses.name: Calculus 1 for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Develops differentiation, its scientific applications, and introductory integration.

category_review.locator: MATH 1341 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Limits, differentiation, integration and the fundamental theorem of calculus are the central content.

courses.name: General Chemistry for Science Majors
courses.description: Introduces chemical structure, reactions, kinetics and thermodynamics with biological applications.

category_review.locator: CHEM 1161 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Chemical bonding, molecular interactions, kinetics and thermodynamics establish chemical-science content, with living systems as examples.

courses.name: Lab for CHEM 1161
courses.description: Develops laboratory techniques for studying chemical and physical processes.

category_review.locator: CHEM 1162 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The lab teaches chemical laboratory techniques, analysis and chemical/physical processes accompanying CHEM 1161.

courses.name: Recitation for CHEM 1161
courses.description: Provides guided practice applying concepts from general chemistry lectures.

category_review.locator: CHEM 1163 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The zero-hour recitation applies the chemical concepts of the accompanying CHEM 1161 lecture.

courses.name: Physics for Life Sciences 1
courses.description: Applies mechanics, fluids and thermal physics to life and health sciences.

category_review.locator: PHYS 1145 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Mechanics, fluids, temperature and kinetic theory are studied through life- and health-science physical problems; the substantive subject is physical science, not mathematical theory alone.

courses.name: Lab for PHYS 1145
courses.description: Investigates introductory life-science physics through laboratory experiments.

category_review.locator: PHYS 1146 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The laboratory experiments accompany the explicitly reviewed mechanics, fluids and thermal-physics content of PHYS 1145.

courses.name: Physics for Engineering 1
courses.description: Develops calculus-based mechanics and fluid physics for engineering.
courses.prerequisites: MATH 1241 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1251 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1340 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1341 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 21EM with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1342 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 211M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 2321 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 316M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: PHYS 1151 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course studies Newtonian mechanics, motion, forces, energy and fluids in engineering physics; calculus is a tool for physical problems, not the principal subject.

courses.name: Lab for PHYS 1151
courses.description: Investigates introductory engineering physics through laboratory experiments.

category_review.locator: PHYS 1152 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Experiments accompany PHYS 1151 engineering mechanics and fluids; the laboratory subject is physical science.

courses.name: Interactive Learning Seminar for PHYS 1151
courses.description: Practices mathematical problem solving in mechanics and fluids.

category_review.locator: PHYS 1153 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The seminar solves physical mechanics, equilibrium, dynamics and fluids problems accompanying PHYS 1151; mathematical techniques support those physical models.

courses.name: Physics 1
courses.description: Develops calculus-based mechanics and fluids with applications across sciences.
courses.prerequisites: MATH 1241 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1251 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1341 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 21EM (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1342 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 211M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 2321 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 316M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: PHYS 1161 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The lecture studies mechanics, fluids and physical principles through science and medicine examples; it is substantive physics despite calculus prerequisites.

courses.name: Lab for PHYS 1161
courses.description: Investigates introductory physics concepts through laboratory experiments.

category_review.locator: PHYS 1162 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Experiments accompany the PHYS 1161 mechanics-and-fluids lecture and remain physical-science laboratory practice.

courses.name: First-Year Writing
courses.description: Develops research and writing across audiences and genres through workshop practice.

category_review.locator: ENGW 1111 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The workshop teaches rhetorical choices, research-based writing, audience awareness and revision in academic, professional and public communication.

courses.name: First-Year Writing for Multilingual Writers
courses.description: Develops research, revision and writing practices with attention to multilingual writers.

category_review.locator: ENGW 1102 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The description teaches writing, rhetorical choices and communication across audiences and genres, with support for multilingual writers; it is not programming.

courses.name: Advanced Writing in the Technical Professions
courses.description: Develops research and communication in technical and professional genres.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

category_review.locator: ENGW 3302 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Technical reports, proposals and presentations are the genres used to teach audience analysis, critical research and revision; the subject is technical communication rather than engineering methods.

courses.name: Advanced Writing in the Environmental Professions
courses.description: Develops environmental research reports through staged writing and revision.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

category_review.locator: ENGW 3303 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Environmental concerns supply the context for instruction in analytic reports, audience analysis, source evaluation and written communication.

courses.name: Advanced Writing in the Sciences
courses.description: Develops scientific argument, evidence presentation and research-based writing.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

category_review.locator: ENGW 3307 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course analyzes how scientific texts present claims and evidence and teaches scientific writing and revision; quantitative evidence is a communication object, not the primary mathematical subject.

courses.name: Interdisciplinary Advanced Writing in the Disciplines
courses.description: Develops research, revision and writing across disciplinary contexts.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

category_review.locator: ENGW 3315 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Interdisciplinary professional, public and academic writing is taught through audience analysis, critical research, peer review and revision.

courses.name: Advanced Machine Learning
courses.description: Studies advanced learning methods and their mathematical and computational foundations.
courses.prerequisites: DS 4400 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4420 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Advanced learning algorithms, structured-data models, Bayesian estimation and generative models are explicitly machine-learning content.

courses.name: Recitation for PHYS 1161
courses.description: Provides guided problem solving for introductory physics.

category_review.locator: PHYS 1163 course block, including explicitly accompanying lecture and concurrent registration evidence
category_review.rationale: The recitation supports interactive problem solving for the reviewed mechanics and fluids of PHYS 1161; zero credit hours do not erase its distinct course identity.

courses.name: Lab for EECE 2322
courses.description: Designs, simulates and tests a computer system using programmable logic.

category_review.locator: EECE 2323 course block and reciprocal EECE 2322 corequisite
category_review.rationale: The laboratory designs, implements, simulates and tests a computer system on programmable logic using a hardware-description language.
